reviews.title: Hidden Subscriptions
reviews.text: If you cancel your subscription through the app, make sure you cancel it on the website too or you might unknowingly get charged for years, and they will refuse a refund even if you have not accessed or had the app downloaded during the subscription period and thought you cancelled it through the app. My receipts for this subscription were being sent to my spam folder in my email, and was not showing up in my Apple subscriptions, and could only see this subscription on their website that I was unaware existed outside the app. I was immediately denied a refund when I caught this charge on my bank account, and told I purchased the subscription on the website I didn’t know existed. My card info was being updated after getting a new card when my old one expired. I’ve never had an experience with a subscription through an app before like this, and never had it so hidden that I was seemingly subscribed to an app before. Unhappy with the app and its quality, which made me cancel and delete the app after the first two weeks. Unhappy with this seemingly intentional hidden subscription compared to other apps, and unhappy with the refund request system that will deny you a refund at the start of a year long subscription you have zero intention of using or accessing. They’ll keep your money even if you don’t want or use the app, and don’t care about how that negatively impacts your financial situation at the moment. Deeply disappointed by this app.

reviews.title: Longtime user, disappointed by the direction
reviews.text:
I have used Videoleap since it first came out, back when it was one of the best mobile video editing apps available. It was clean, useful, creative, and reasonably priced. I recommended it because it felt like the developers actually listened to customers and focused on making a great editing tool.

Unfortunately, the app has changed. It now feels far too commercial, overloaded with unnecessary AI features, templates, upsells, and subscription pressure. Instead of building all of this into the original app, there should have been a separate Pro version for users who wanted those extras, while longtime users could keep the solid editor we originally supported.

The pricing is the biggest disappointment. I remember when there was a bundle option around $50. Now I am seeing $9.99 per week for Pro, $4.99 per week for Lite, and $119.99 per year. Compared with the old $50 option, the yearly plan is about a 140% increase. Paying $9.99 every week for a mobile editing app is ridiculous, especially when CapCut in the US can be used for about $9 a month and offers as much or more value.

Videoleap used to feel like an app made for creators. Now it feels like greed and constant monetization took over. I hope the developers listen again, because this used to be a great app. Sorry cannot recommend anymore.
